problem: LLM-based VLN methods that turn observations into text captions and summaries suffer from hallucination, noisy captions, weak spatial understanding and poor long-horizon reasoning. Fine-tuned foundation-model VLN agents still lag specialized VLN systems.
motivation: Text-only foundation-model navigation shows a large gap to specialized VLN models on R2R, and fine-tuning can hurt general language ability. The paper argues that humans navigate by identifying key visual landmarks and keeping a global topological memory, so the agent should ground reasoning in salient references and use a topological map.
key_idea: Augment a frozen InstructBLIP (Q-Former + FlanT5 encoder-decoder) with a graph-based historical topology memory decoded with graph-aware self-attention, and use multi-curvature (Euclidean/hyperbolic/spherical) spatiotemporal scoring to pick visual references for chain-of-thought reasoning.
insight: Ablations on R2R val-unseen (Table 4) show the historical topology encoding is essential: without it SR falls from 73 to 18. Removing the multi-curvature manifold reference filtering gives the largest drop among the other modules (SR 73 to 69, SPL 60 to 55), while removing the local image branch or Q-Former training matters less. Gains over DUET grow as training data shrinks (10% data: 65 vs 48 SR), which suggests the foundation-model prior improves data efficiency.
method: Q-Former dual-branch encoding: InstructBLIP Q-Former with 32 learnable queries attends to instructions and view features to produce image tokens for the LLM; a second branch matches detection boxes and segmentation masks by IoU and reads average depth to get object-agent distances.

Multi-curvature manifold reference selection: nouns from instructions form Λx; temporal scores (cosine distance between consecutive mean-pooled panoramic features) and spatial uniqueness scores (object present only in the chosen action view) are multiplied and thresholded to add references Λv. Scores are computed in Euclidean, hyperbolic (tanh exp-map) and spherical spaces and summed (Eq. 9).

Visual-reference chain-of-thought: the LLM decoder generates reasoning anchored on the selected landmarks; the Q-Former and projection are fine-tuned on autoregressively generated navigation reasoning data from R2R train.

Historical topology graph memory: incrementally built graph of visited, navigable and current nodes plus a stop node. Node embeddings are pooled view features plus direction, step and action embeddings, then passed through self-attention.

Graph-Aware Self-Attention (GASA): cross-attention with LLM-encoded instructions, then self-attention with a learnable pairwise-distance bias term (Ewe+be); an FFN outputs node scores, the top unvisited node is chosen and reached via shortest path.

Two-stage training: stage 1 fine-tunes only the Q-Former (200k steps, batch 8, lr 1e-5); stage 2 fine-tunes only the policy network with the VLM frozen, using L = ς·L_bc + L_DAG (imitation plus DAgger-style pseudo-labels from partial graphs).

setting.backbone: InstructBLIP (ViT-g/14 + Q-Former + FlanT5-XL/XXL), frozen LLM and visual encoder, plus trained topology policy network
setting.training_data: R2R train set (plus navigation-reasoning data generated from R2R train); PREVALENT pretrained features mentioned as a starting point; no extra augmentation data
setting.observation: panoramic multi-view RGB images with candidate directions, plus depth for object distances and object detection/segmentation
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (select a node/angle among candidates, with a stop node)
setting.privileged: none (navigation graph connectivity is given as in standard R2R)

numbers.extra: trained on R2R train only, no extra pretraining data

numbers_note: Table 3 (data-volume ablation) shows different values for the 100% data rows (e.g. 5B val-unseen SR 72, SPL 61, NE 3.15) than Tables 1-2 (SR 74, SPL 63); the paper does not explain the discrepancy. Main results are taken from Tables 1-2.
results: On R2R val-unseen the 5B model reaches SR 74 / SPL 63 / NE 2.92, beating the strongest foundation-model baseline NaviLLM (SR 67, SPL 59). It also beats DUET without pretraining (SR 64, SPL 55). It stays below pretraining/data-scaled methods such as GOAT (SR 77, SPL 68) and DUET+ScaleVLN (SR 79, SPL 70).
limitations: Evaluated only on R2R (discrete nav graph, Matterport3D); no continuous-environment, other-benchmark or real-robot tests, and no hallucination measurement beyond qualitative visualizations.
Still below methods with large-scale pretraining or data augmentation (GOAT, ScaleVLN); Table 3 full-data numbers are inconsistent with Tables 1-2.
The topology graph relies on provided navigation graph connectivity, and the pipeline needs detection/segmentation/depth modules plus a two-stage training procedure.
